title: Engine: exposure that can darken, glow retune, fog cap and a dimmer horizon (fix the desert/snow flashbang)
player_outcome: On medium, high and ultra the desert and snow read like on low: bright but never a white wash. Leaving a cave adapts in under a second with no flashbang, and caves still brighten slowly as the eyes adjust. Every preset gets the same cave adaptation.
design: GraphicsSettings.Load: load and validate LightingConfig (throw on problems like graphics.json) and expose GraphicsSettings.Lighting.

EnvironmentController.Initialize: take glow from config. Set GlowNormalized = true, GlowHdrThreshold = Threshold, GlowHdrScale = Softness, GlowIntensity, GlowHdrLuminanceCap and SetGlowLevel(i, Levels[i]), replacing lines 60-64 and 90. SsilIntensity and VolumetricFogAlbedo come from ScreenSpace.

EnvironmentController.ApplyPreset: when p.AutoExposure, set AutoExposureMinSensitivity/MaxSensitivity from ExposureModel.AutoWindow, AutoExposureScale = AutoKey and AutoExposureSpeed = AutoSpeed, replacing 85/170/0.35/0.3 at lines 94-97.

New partial game/Ambience/EnvironmentController.Exposure.cs. It holds ExposureModel _exposure and float _biomeExposure; BlendBiome eases _biomeExposure toward Biome?.ExposureBias ?? 1 with the existing k.

The new partial exposes public float Exposure => _exposure.Current and void UpdateExposure(float dt), called at the end of Apply. UpdateExposure computes Target(_outdoor, Daylight, _biomeExposure), steps the model, and writes _camera.ExposureMultiplier only when the value moved by more than 0.002 (no per-frame RenderingServer churn).

EnvironmentController.Frame.UpdateFog: FogDepthBegin = Lerp(Min(reach * 0.3, Fog.NearCap / Max(_biomeDensity, 0.5)), 2, deep). Today it is about 149-178 m on medium and higher, so distant sand is unfogged.

shaders/horizon.gdshader, land branch: clamp the albedo luminance so distant sand and snow cannot outshine the streamed terrain (float l = dot(base, vec3(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722)); base *= min(1.0, 0.42 / max(l, 1e-3))) and set AO = 0.8 instead of 1.0. Water is unchanged.

New tour game/Testing/Tours/lighting.cmds: time 12; for each preset in low/medium/high/ultra (graphics <preset>) take noon screenshots at spawn forest, biome desert and biome tundra, then a tp cave underground shot.

New tools/ci/shot_stats.py (Pillow + numpy, about 70 lines). For each PNG it prints mean Rec.709 luma, the percentage of pixels with luma > 0.98, and with --profile a 12-bin luma profile along the horizontal centre line.
docs/architecture/rendering.md: update the light-model table rows for exposure and glow, and the preset paragraph.
files_modify: game/Ambience/EnvironmentController.cs — glow/SSIL/volumetric from config, AE window in ApplyPreset
game/Ambience/EnvironmentController.Frame.cs — call UpdateExposure, fog near cap, blend biome exposure
data_changes: Tune data/config/lighting.json exposure/glow values from the tour results (the code keeps no constants)
tests: basic.cmds, after the arena section: 'time noon' / 'fill -11 -3 -11 11 9 11 stone' / 'fill -10 0 -10 10 7 10 air' / 'wait 4' / 'assert render.exposure > 1.3' (sealed room adapts) / 'fill -10 8 -10 10 9 10 air' / 'wait 1.5' / 'assert render.exposure < 1.15' (open sky darkens quickly) / 'assert errors == 0'
Core ExposureModelTests from P1-02 cover the logic; there is no engine unit test
verification: Headless smoke basic.cmds prints SMOKE PASS (the exposure model runs without a renderer).

python3 tools/ci/shot_stats.py shots/*.png: desert and tundra clipped < 2% on medium/high/ultra, and their mean luma within ±15% of the low preset's; forest on medium within +25% of low; cave mean luma on low and medium >= the old baseline (compare with a pre-change run)
Manual: walk out of a cave into the desert at noon on ultra; the image settles in under 1 s and never goes white
risks: Godot applies CameraAttributes.ExposureMultiplier and auto-exposure before the glow threshold. Check that flames and lava still bloom after the threshold rise (flame albedo peaks around 2.8 HDR) and lower Glow.Threshold if not.
lavapipe is slow: run only lighting.cmds (about 20 shots), not the full tour.
Headless has no auto-exposure, so render.exposure checks only the CPU model part.
